Chosen over src.utils.db_locking.db_write_lock, which is an in-process asyncio/thread lock scoped to one Python process and structurally cannot serialize a second OS process (this runner is a separate process from the 3 writer services). acquire_cleanup_lease is also what the existing P2.2 storage_lifecycle_runner.py already uses for the identical 'one cleanup process at a time' requirement, so this is the established cross-process idiom in this codebase, not a new primitive.

eligibility_contract.rule: A transfer_index row is archival-ELIGIBLE only if ALL of: (1) block_time is a valid positive number older than the frozen 90-day hot_boundary_unix, (2) classify() does not return hot_pinned (destination in creator_funders.creator_address, OR source/destination in wt_ops_v2.operator_entities.entity_address, OR signature in local_operation_discovery_corpus.db's direct_funding_edges.funding_signature/upstream_edges.upstream_signature), (3) classify() does not return hot_ambiguous (NULL/non-numeric/<=0 block_time is held HOT, never archived -- fail-closed on ambiguity), (4) the row is not already represented in an existing COLD month segment by composite identity (signature, source, destination) -- checked via _existing_cold_signatures() against the target month's segment file before every COLD copy.
eligibility_contract.90_day_boundary_value: HOT_RETENTION_DAYS = 90, matching src/scripts/cleanup_transfers.py's TransferIndexCleanup(retention_days=90) -- unchanged, not re-derived.
eligibility_contract.pin_dimensions_verified_by_grep: PinSets(...) construction pattern confirmed in tests/test_storage_lifecycle_p5b_stage2_parts7_21.py; derive_pin_sets() in the new runner queries creator_funders.creator_address, wt_ops_v2.db operator_entities.entity_address, and local_operation_discovery_corpus.db direct_funding_edges.funding_signature + upstream_edges.upstream_signature -- table/column names verified against the live databases during Part 18 census, not assumed.

pipeline_sequence: 1. READ: plain SELECT (id-bounded keyset batch) against a mode=ro HOT connection. No write lock ever taken in this phase.

2. CLASSIFY: p5b_delta_reconciler.classify() per row against a frozen PinSets (derived fresh at run start from live creator_funders/operator_entities/discovery-corpus tables, never cached across runs).
3. DEDUPE-AGAINST-COLD: identity check (signature) against the target month's existing COLD segment file, skipping rows already represented.
4. COLD COPY: INSERT OR IGNORE into a per-month rolling-accumulation segment file (created via create_cold_segment() if absent). No HOT lock required -- entirely separate files.

5. VERIFY: fresh read-only re-open of each touched COLD segment, composite-identity set comparison against what was selected for that batch. Any missing row aborts the WHOLE run (fail-closed) before any HOT mutation -- the just-written COLD data is left in place (immutable, safe, not rolled back).

6. HOT RETIREMENT (real-retire mode only): acquire_cleanup_lease (non-blocking) -> BEGIN IMMEDIATE -> DELETE FROM transfer_index WHERE id IN (<exact ids from this verified batch>) -> COMMIT -> release lease. On CleanupLeaseHeldError or sqlite3.OperationalError (SQLITE_BUSY/locked), the batch aborts cleanly; already-copied+verified COLD data is retained for a later run to retire.
segment_strategy: Rolling per-calendar-month accumulation (transfer_index_cold_<YYYY>_<MM>.sqlite), matching the existing convention in database/_p5a_migration_build/cold_segments/. A batch may span >1 month near a boundary; rows are grouped and appended to each relevant month's file. Chosen over one-segment-per-run (would fragment into hundreds of tiny segments given the ~500-row batch size) and one-segment-per-batch (same problem, worse). Segments are NOT closed by the runner automatically every batch -- close_segment() (manifest finalization + sha256 digest + registry visibility) is a deliberate later step, consistent with P4's contract that a segment must be explicitly closed before ColdSegmentRegistry treats it as qualified; the activation contract specifies when production closure happens.

default_safe_design.no_args_or_dry_run: zero writes anywhere -- --dry-run peeks at batches via a read-only connection, classifies, reports counts, and never persists a checkpoint or COLD row.
default_safe_design.copy_verify_only: writes COLD, verifies, never deletes HOT -- available via --copy-verify-only, and structurally wins over confirm_retire even if both are passed.
default_safe_design.real_retirement_double_gate: requires BOTH --confirm-retire-hot-rows-in-production (CLI flag / confirm_retire=True) AND the environment variable HOT_COLD_ROLLOVER_CONFIRM=YES-RETIRE-PRODUCTION-HOT-ROWS. Missing either gate silently falls back to COPY_VERIFY_ONLY_UNCONFIRMED mode (zero HOT deletions), never an error that could be silenced/bypassed by a misconfigured flag alone.
